questions.stem: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 at Bombay. Who was the Scottish-born British civil servant who played the key role in its founding?
questions.explanation: Allan Octavian HUME (1829-1912) — retired British ICS officer, called the 'Father of the Indian National Congress' — organised the first INC session (28-31 Dec 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay; 72 delegates from across India). Acted as its first General Secretary. Wedderburn, Yule, Cotton were all sympathetic British who served as INC presidents — the only Britons to preside: George YULE (1888, first non-Indian president), William WEDDERBURN (1889 & 1910), Alfred WEBB (1894), Henry COTTON (1904), Annie BESANT (Irish-born, 1917 — first woman). Dadabhai Naoroji's 1886 presidential address established INC as a national body. INC had 3 phases: MODERATE (1885-1905) → EXTREMIST (1905-1917) → GANDHIAN (1917-1947).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Dadabhai Naoroji is famously known as the 'Grand Old Man of India' and presided over the INC three times. Which year did he FIRST articulate the demand for 'SWARAJ' (self-government) as the political objective of INC?
questions.explanation: DADABHAI NAOROJI (1825-1917) — presided over INC 3 times (1886 Calcutta, 1893 Lahore, 1906 CALCUTTA — where in his presidential address he publicly demanded 'SWARAJ' for the FIRST TIME in a clearly-articulated form). Author of 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) — pioneer of the DRAIN THEORY showing how Britain bled wealth from India. First Indian elected to the British Parliament — Liberal MP for Finsbury Central, London (1892-95). The 1906 session is also notable for the growing Moderate-Extremist split, which would boil over at the 1907 SURAT SPLIT. Tilak's 'Swaraj is my birthright' slogan came in 1916 during the Home Rule Movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The famous 'Surat Split' of the INC in 1907 was a formal division between which two factions?
questions.explanation: The SURAT SPLIT (Dec 1907 at Surat, Gujarat) formally divided the Congress into two factions: MODERATES led by Gopal Krishna GOKHALE + Pherozeshah MEHTA + Dadabhai Naoroji — favouring prayer-petition-protest, gradual reforms; EXTREMISTS led by the TRIO 'LAL-BAL-PAL' (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal) + Aurobindo Ghosh — wanting militancy, boycott, swadeshi, Swaraj. Trigger: Surat session presidency choice — Moderates wanted Rashbehari Ghose; Extremists wanted Tilak. Reunion at LUCKNOW 1916 session (under Ambika Charan Mazumdar), which ALSO saw the HC Pact with the Muslim League. The 1905 Bengal Partition had catalysed Extremist rise; Moderates faded post-1916. Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal — 'Lal-Bal-Pal'.

questions.stem: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded which society in 1905, aimed at training Indians to serve the motherland in a self-less manner?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna GOKHALE (1866-1915) — called Mahatma Gandhi's 'POLITICAL GURU' — founded the SERVANTS OF INDIA SOCIETY in 1905 in Pune. Aim: to train national missionaries for the service of India and to promote the interests of the Indian people by constitutional means. Gokhale presided over the 1905 Benares session of INC. Also: Gokhale drafted the ELEMENTARY EDUCATION BILL 1911 (defeated in Council). Other similar societies: Ramakrishna Mission (Swami Vivekananda, 1897), Arya Samaj (Dayanand Saraswati, 1875), Theosophical Society (Blavatsky/Olcott, 1875 US; Annie Besant brought it to prominence in India), Prarthana Samaj (Atmaram Pandurang, 1867 Bombay — Ranade, Bhandarkar active), Brahmo Samaj (Raja Rammohan Roy, 1828), Hindu Mahasabha (Madan Mohan Malaviya, 1915).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Bal Gangadhar Tilak popularised the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it'. During which movement/occasion was this famously declared?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar TILAK (1856-1920, 'Lokmanya') coined 'SWARAJYA MAZHA JANMA SIDDHA HAKKA AHE ANI TO MI MILAVANARACH' (Marathi) — 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' — during the Home Rule Movement (1916), which he launched from Pune in April 1916. Annie Besant launched a parallel Home Rule League from Madras in Sept 1916. Both Leagues merged with the INC effectively by 1918. Tilak started the newspapers KESARI (Marathi) and MAHRATTA (English) in 1881. Promoted GANESH UTSAV (1893) and SHIVAJI UTSAV (1895) as mass mobilisation tools. Jailed multiple times; wrote 'Gita Rahasya' (1915) in Mandalay prison. Died on 1 August 1920 — the day Non-Cooperation was formally launched.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The historic 1929 LAHORE session of the INC, where 'PURNA SWARAJ' (Complete Independence) was declared as the goal, was presided by:
questions.explanation: JAWAHARLAL NEHRU (1889-1964), aged 40, became the YOUNGEST INC President at the LAHORE session (December 1929). At midnight of 31 December 1929, the TRICOLOUR was unfurled on the banks of the Ravi river, and the Purna Swaraj resolution was passed — declaring COMPLETE INDEPENDENCE as the ultimate goal. 26 JANUARY 1930 was observed as the first INDEPENDENCE DAY nationwide (celebrated annually till 1947 as 'Purna Swaraj Day'). Upon independence, 26 Jan 1950 was deliberately chosen as REPUBLIC DAY (when Constitution came into force) to honour this legacy. MOTILAL NEHRU (JLN's father) had presided INC in 1919 and 1928 (when the Nehru Report was finalised). SC Bose presided in 1938 Haripura and 1939 Tripuri (led to his split with Gandhi).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885. Who was its first President?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee presided over the first INC session in Bombay (1885).

questions.stem: Who founded the Indian National Congress?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Allan Octavian (A.O.) Hume, a retired ICS officer, founded the INC in consultation with Lord Dufferin.

questions.stem: The 'safety-valve theory' regarding the founding of the INC attributes the British support to:

options.option_text: Providing a platform for moderate Indians to vent grievances peacefully
Encouraging Indians to join the British army
Creating a legislative council for India

questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai and others later argued Hume founded INC as a 'safety valve' to channel educated Indian discontent away from rebellion.

questions.stem: Who presented the theory of 'Economic Drain' (Drain of Wealth) from India to Britain?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji, in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901), systematically argued that British policies drained India's wealth.

questions.stem: Dadabhai Naoroji was elected to the British House of Commons in 1892 from which constituency?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Naoroji was elected Liberal MP for Finsbury Central (London) in 1892 — first Indian MP in British Parliament.

questions.stem: Which period is broadly considered the 'Moderate Phase' of the Indian National Congress?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: 1885–1905 is the Moderate Phase; demands were constitutional, methods were petitions/memorials, goals were self-governance within Empire.

questions.stem: The Moderates' primary method of political agitation was:

options.option_text: Prayers, petitions and resolutions to the British Parliament

questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Moderate leaders like Gokhale believed in constitutional methods: petitions, resolutions, press campaigns, and delegations to London.

questions.stem: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded which political organisation to train moderate nationalists?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society (1905) to train self-sacrificing workers for nation-building.

questions.stem: Which Congress session of 1906 is notable for passing resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: The 1906 Calcutta Session under Dadabhai Naoroji passed four resolutions (Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education) reflecting Extremist influence.

questions.stem: The Surat Split of 1907 divided the Indian National Congress into Moderates and Extremists. Who led the Extremists?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak led the Extremists at Surat; the split occurred over the choice of Congress President and ideological differences.

questions.stem: Which Moderate leader wrote 'New Lamps for Old' criticising the early nationalist methods?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Aurobindo Ghose wrote the series 'New Lamps for Old' (1893) criticising Moderate politics, advocating more aggressive nationalism.

questions.stem: The partition of Bengal (1905) was annulled in which year?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon's 1905 Partition of Bengal was reversed in 1911 (announced at the Delhi Durbar); Bengal was reunited.

questions.stem: Surendranath Banerjea founded the Indian Association in Calcutta in which year?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Surendranath Banerjea founded the Indian Association (1876) in Calcutta as a precursor organisation to the INC.

questions.stem: The Moderates supported the Indian Councils Act of 1892 (also called Minto-Morley reforms?) No — which Act did Moderates acclaim as a step forward?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: The Indian Councils Act 1892 expanded legislative councils and allowed limited budget discussions — welcomed by the Moderate Congress as progress.

questions.stem: Who coined the phrase 'Poverty is not a virtue' while arguing against British economic policies in India?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji's economic writings systematically documented the poverty caused by British revenue extraction and drain.

questions.stem: M.G. Ranade was associated with which reform society in Maharashtra?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: Mahadev Govind Ranade (economist and Moderate leader) was a founder of the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay (1867).

questions.stem: Which annual session of the Indian National Congress first demanded 'Swaraj' as a goal?
questions.subject: History
questions.explanation: The 1906 Calcutta session under Naoroji passed the Swaraj resolution; though 'complete independence' was only declared at Lahore 1929.
